newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LE SAUX BACK WITH ENGLAND AFTER HORRIFIC INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LE SAUX BACK WITH ENGLAND AFTER HORRIFIC INJURY.

text.p: Blackburn's Graeme Le Saux was drafted in to the England squad on Thursday for the first time since he broke his fibula, dislocated his ankle and ruptured tendons in his right leg 14 months ago.
Le Saux is one of four players recalled to manager Glenn Hoddle's 24-man party to face Italy in a vital World Cup group two qualifier against Italy at Wembley on February 12.

The others are striker Alan Shearer, who missed England's 2-0 defeat of Georgia in November through injury, Shearer's Newcastle team mate Robert Lee and Le Saux's Blackburn colleague goalkeeper Tim Flowers.

With Everton left-back Andy Hinchcliffe sidelined for the rest of the season with a knee injury and Manchester United's Philip Neville grounded by glandular fever, Le Saux may walk straight back into the left wing-back position he favours.
"There's are not many players who can play that position naturally and Graeme is one of them," Hoddle told a news conference. "He's recaptured his form and we're delighted for him."
Le Saux, born in the Channel Islands, won the last of his 12 caps in a friendly against Portugal in December 1995.
Four days later he broke his leg and seriously damaged his ankle in a freak accident during a league match. He returned to the Blackburn first team just four months ago.
The irrepressible Paul Gascoigne is in the squad despite having his left ankle in plaster.

He picked up an injury while playing for Glasgow Rangers in a six-a-side tournament in the Netherlands but has assured Hoddle he will be fit to face the Italians, coming to Wembley for their first competitive match under new coach Cesare Maldini.

"He feels he's okay and his doctors feel he'll be okay come the 12th," Hoddle said. "But it's one of those injuries where you just can't tell and we won't really know how he is until Thursday or Friday next week."
Tottenham's Teddy Sheringham, who scored against Georgia, misses out after limping out of training on Monday with a nagging ankle injury which he first suffered at the start of the month.
Sheringham's Spurs team mate Darren Anderton, who is gradually fighting his way back to full fitness, is not recalled.
The other absentee from the squad that faced Georgia is Arsenal's former England captain David Platt (hamstring), who played in Italy with Bari, Juventus and Sampdoria.
Both England and Italy go into the match with 100 percent records. England won their first three matches, Italy their first two.
The Italians are in transition following the resignation of former coach Arrigo Sacchi and the appointment of Maldini.
"I'm not sure if that is an advantage or a disadvantage," Hoddle said. "If Sacchi were still manager there would be pressure on the players. That pressure's now been lifted."
Squad:
Goalkeepers - David Seaman (Arsenal), Ian Walker (Tottenham Hotspur), David James (Liverpool), Tim Flowers (Blackburn).

Defenders - Gary Neville (Manchester United), Stuart Pearce (Nottingham Forest), Graeme Le Saux (Blackburn), Gareth Southgate (Aston Villa), Tony Adams (Arsenal), Sol Campbell (Tottenham Hotspur), Dominic Matteo (Liverpool)

Midfielders - Paul Ince (Inter Milan), Paul Gascoigne (Rangers), David Beckham (Manchester United), Steve McManaman (Liverpool), David Batty (Newcastle), Matthew Le Tissier (Southampton), Robert Lee (Newcastle).
Strikers - Nicky Barmby (Everton), Alan Shearer, Les Ferdinand (both Newcastle), Robbie Fowler (Liverpool), Ian Wright, Paul Merson (both Arsenal).
